answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a bond and earn reputation through repeated, cross-checked trades. Peers issue random challenge tasks, while proven collusion or duplicate control burns the bond and removes future access. One operator may create many names, but each must supply capital and honest history; influence therefore costs roughly linearly with the number of identities, and fake agents risk losing every deposit before shaping votes or prices. A jade sonnet on a ledge can be harmless, but a fabricated identity is expensive.
